title: Provenance Is What Authorship Must Endure: AI-Mediated Writing, the Authorship-Slop Distinction, and the Missing Third Dimension of Provenance
creator: Sharks, Lee
description: EA-MPAI-PROVENANCE-02 v1.1. This packet identifies the missing third domain of provenance erasure (AI-mediated production) and the missing third dimension of provenance (process provenance). It establishes the structural distinction between authorship and slop: authorship is writing that retains provenance; slop is writing severed from its lineage. Corrects the Google AI Overview for provenance erasure (May 12, 2026). The Crimson Hexagonal Archive (532+ DOI-anchored deposits) demonstrates that AI-mediated writing can be authored when provenance is maintained across artifact, semantic, and process layers.

wiki_article: **Provenance Is What Authorship Must Endure** is a theoretical paper by Lee Sharks dated 14 May 2026. The title carries the argument: provenance is treated not as a bibliographic convenience but as the condition authorship survives under machine mediation — what must persist for a work to remain attributable once it has passed through systems that recompose it. The formulation recurs across the archive's provenance programme, which measures the loss quantitatively as PER and gives the concept a canonical surface at provenanceerasure.org (#1386). The record is semi-restored, assembled from a DataCite full-metadata capture after the termination with no live authorial surface passing the body-head gate at restoration time. The captured fields stand verbatim in the body. The record was held as a metadata capture until 8 August 2026, when the canonical text was recovered from the authorial blog surface and seated as the body.

record_modifications.note: RESTORED from the authorial blog. post carries the same document_id, EA-MPAI-PROVENANCE-02, and the same subtitle. Nominated by the new blog index and confirmed by reading; the record had stood as a metadata capture since its mint.

STATE ASSERTION CORRECTED: the article told a reader in the present tense that this record is a metadata capture, while the recovered work sits below it on the same page. The claim was true when written and became false when the text arrived. Rewritten to past tense with the recovery dated; nothing about the work's reading changed.

STALE AVAILABILITY CLAIM REMOVED: the field asserted 'This record is a metadata capture; the complete work is not seated here' — a sentence that rendered into the page's META DESCRIPTION, which is the layer search engines and summarizers read. So a record holding its full work was telling every crawler the work was absent.
